title: Tracking queen constraints with three Boolean arrays
summary: Use the column array cols and diagonal arrays diags1 and diags2, mapped from zero-based row and column coordinates, to record and check queen occupancy.
context: This figure matches the code implementation: on a 4×4 board (n = 4), row index row increases top to bottom and column index col increases left to right, both starting at 0 (zero-based indexing). The queen shown sits at zero-based coordinates (1, 1) (the second row and second column); in the Boolean arrays, T denotes occupied and F denotes free.
description: Squares on the same main diagonal share the same row − col, and squares on the same antidiagonal share the same row + col. A candidate square (row, col) looks up the three arrays at col, row − col + n − 1, and row + col; a queen can be placed there only if all three entries are F. When n = 4, row − col ranges from −3 to 3, and adding 3 maps it to nonnegative indices 0 through 6.

Placing a queen sets the three corresponding entries to T, and backtracking restores them to F. The two tables below list the indexing rules and the complete values of the three arrays shown in the figure.

frames.title: Tracking queen constraints with three Boolean arrays
frames.explanation: With the three Boolean arrays cols, diags1, and diags2, column and diagonal conflicts can be checked in constant time; in general, an n×n board has n columns, with 2n − 1 main diagonals and antidiagonals each.
